name: Filesystem Security and Compliance Scan (external statement)
description: Run a Trivy scan on the local file system to detect vulnerabilities, secrets, and misconfigurations, for a customer-facing assurance statement.

reporting.expectedOutput: Allowlisted assurance statement, released only for a clean assessment

notes: Sibling of sample_intent_fs_scan_management.json with the same target and parameters, but criteria narrowed to nis2 alone. Expect this one to produce no artifact: on the observed scan the worstSeverity is CRITICAL, so project_external returns {"released": false, "withheldBecause": ["assessment found a CRITICAL-severity result; an external statement is only produced for a clean assessment"], ...} carrying no findings, no paths and no package identifiers. That is the intended outcome, not a failure — the honest external output for an assessment that found something is nothing rather than a softened version. A 'clean' result means nothing found at HIGH or CRITICAL (Trivy's constant severity filter), which is why a released statement must carry the scope that qualifies it — 'no findings' without that bound reads as a broader claim than the scan made. For the case where the gate opens, see sample_intent_python_scan_external_release.json.
